newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury urges Saudi fiscal discipline.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury urges Saudi fiscal discipline.

text.p: Saudi Arabia should "bring its fiscal house in order" and loosen its rules for foreign investment to strengthen its economy, Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said Thursday.

In remarks prepared for delivery to the US-Saudi Business Council, Summers said fiscal discipline was "particularly important" for Saudi Arabia because fluctuations in oil prices have such an impact on its finances.
"Over the long term, only by pursuing a policy of fiscal soundness can any country, the United States or any other, lay the foundation for continued growth," Summers said.
Higher oil prices this year have reduced pressures on Saudi Arabia's budget, but that progress could quickly be undone if prices came down, Summers said.
Saudi Arabia gets 75 percent of its government revenues from oil, which accounts for 90 percent of its exports, Summers noted, adding it needs to develop a more broadly based economy.
"However, a strategy to fully diversify Saudi Arabia's economy must also include investment reform, since investments are the key to diversifying the Kingdon's economy," Summers said.
He suggested that liberalizing trade and investment rules would pay large dividends for Saudi Arabia and noted approvingly that the nation was negotiating for entry to the World Trade Organization.
"I am convinced that Saudi Arabia's accession to the WTO would go a long way to reducing existing trade barriers," Summers said.

He added WTO membership would likely require modifying a pre-shipment and certification program that Saudi Arabia now maintains. Summers said the program "lacks transparency" in its application and does not meet international norms.
